issues.description: Docstring and changelog claim 'real-time pacing' but code only chunks bytes with no timing.
issues.detail: The implementation fixes packet size but sends as fast as _write_frame is called — no sleep, no _next_send_time, no _send_interval gate. If Vonage requires 20ms cadence, this will burst. Either wire pacing through using the existing interval machinery, or correct the documentation to claim only fixed framing.

issues.description: Rename of audio_packet_bytes to fixed_audio_packet_size is a silent breaking change with no deprecation alias.
issues.detail: Existing callers passing the old kwarg will be silently ignored by Pydantic and receive unpacketized audio with no error. Either keep a deprecated alias that emits a warning for one release, or flag this prominently as a breaking change in the upgrade path.

issues.description: Partial tail bytes in the audio send buffer are never flushed and control payloads jump the queue.
issues.detail: The while-loop only emits full packet_bytes chunks; remainder bytes linger indefinitely and are silently dropped at stream end. Worse, if JSON control payloads interleave with PCM, the buffered remainder stays parked while control ships immediately, reversing order on the wire. Add a flush invariant on EndFrame/stop and before control sends.

issues.description: Packetization, serialization, and audio/control discrimination are complected inside _write_frame.
issues.detail: The transport conflates serializer output, isinstance(bytes) type-sniffing to distinguish audio from control JSON, and fixed-size repacketization. The serializer's str|bytes return overloads type with meaning, and the transport re-derives that meaning. A small Packetizer value plus a tagged AudioBytes/ControlText payload would separate framing from transport.

issues.description: fixed_audio_packet_size has no validation — negative, zero, or non-sample-aligned values silently produce garbage.
issues.detail: A negative or non-multiple-of-sample-width value will split 16-bit samples mid-byte or produce infinite empty chunks. Validate >0 and multiple of frame size at TransportParams construction, or document the constraint. Right now it is a foot-gun for any caller who fat-fingers the knob.

issues.description: DTMF parsing accepts two undocumented payload shapes 'just in case' without citing the protocol.
issues.detail: `message.get('digit') or message.get('dtmf', {}).get('digit')` encodes uncertainty about Vonage's actual schema as runtime fallback. Either confirm the spec and delete one branch, or document which Vonage firmware/version emits which shape. As written it reads like speculative cleverness a future maintainer will curse.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the Vonage serializer and FastAPI transport hook are roughly the right shape but ship with overstated documentation and under-specified contracts. The headline issue is that 'real-time pacing' is claimed but not implemented — the code only chunks bytes. The rename of audio_packet_bytes is a silent breaking change, the packet-size knob is unvalidated, and partial tail bytes never flush while control payloads jump ahead of buffered audio. Structurally, packetization is complected with serialization and transport, and DTMF parsing hedges across two undocumented schemas. Needs-work before landing: align docs with behavior, add a deprecation alias, validate inputs, fix the flush/ordering invariant, and add tests.
